padding_attention.reading: The wrap-padded model places 59.4% of its attribution on padded material — audio it manufactured by tiling — against a 67.9% uniform share. The zero-padded model places 10.1% on its padding, correctly ignoring silence. So roughly six times as much of the baseline's evidence comes from copies rather than from the recorded cycle.

band_pointing.reading: Both models attend LESS to the 100-1000 Hz wheeze band when a wheeze is present, and zero-padding does not fix it (-0.053 -> -0.078). The backwards contrast is not a padding artefact.

conclusion: Wrap-padding buys +0.031 official ICBHI and costs attribution quality: 59% of the baseline's evidence lands on tiled copies, and M44's tiling measure shows those copies are NOT treated equivalently (mean r=0.098). Zero-padding produces a cleaner-attending model that scores lower. KEEP wrap-padding as the default — it is field-standard on ICBHI and it wins on the reportable metric — but the paper should state that the gain is partly attributable to padding structure rather than to respiratory acoustics. The backwards wheeze-band contrast survives both schemes and is therefore a property of the model, not of the padding.
open: A fade-in/out tiling variant, used by some published ICBHI implementations to avoid seam discontinuities, was not tested. It is the obvious third arm.
